lead: Selection endpoints outside the visible viewport need explicit rendering/projection so DOM/native selection cannot point into a gap.
evidence: CodeMirror creates extra single-line viewports for anchor/head outside the main viewport.
decision: Keep as proof law; existing huge-document vertical selection and blank-gap rows are the current Slate proof.

lead: Viewport size and actually visible/rendered ranges should be tracked separately.
evidence: CodeMirror exposes `viewport` and `visibleRanges`, and long-line tests assert visible ranges can be smaller than viewport.
decision: Promoted/kept in huge-document benchmark hygiene: report mounted/pending, boundary, materialization, and projected-marker counts instead of reducing DOM budget to one number.
verification: P41 benchmark README/trace audit kept mounted/pending top-level counts, DOM/viewport boundary counts, materialization metrics, and projected selection marker counts.

lead: Viewport measurement should have explicit stabilization and restart limits.
evidence: CodeMirror measure loop restarts until coherent and warns after more than five restarts.
decision: Promote to benchmark/test lead: keep materialization-frame and geometry-change counters visible in huge-doc traces.
verification: P32 browser trace already records materialization frames; future metrics should keep it.

lead: Projected selection layers must redraw on viewport movement and must not render over native selection for the same range.
evidence: CodeMirror hides native selection for drawn selection and redraws selection layer on viewport changes.
decision: Keep as proof law; existing Slate visual rows should keep asserting no double native/projected highlight.
verification: P38 huge-doc visual proof passed; prior selection rows include native/projected agreement checks.

lead: When a focused widget owns native selection, projected-selection logic must not hide, steal, or misclassify that widget selection.
evidence: CodeMirror exposes drawn selection as a native-selection replacement and has a focused-widget exception where native selection must remain visible inside the focused widget.
decision: Promoted to test-packet: Slate editable-void input range selection is visible/native, not mapped as editor visible selection, and not double-highlighted.
verification: `bun run playwright playwright/integration/examples/editable-voids.test.ts --project=chromium --grep "focused editable void input range selection native-owned|ArrowLeft inside editable void input native-owned|ignores selectionchange noise from input inside editable void|restores outer editor selection after editing input inside editable void"` passed 4/4.
